title: Annual Maintain & Mobilize: Ops Bench and Cadence Reset
summary: Leadership all-hands focused on an end-of-year operational reset: clarifying on-call cadence, ops bench (warm standby capacity) for peak events, cross-team handoffs, and a short roadmap of operational priorities for Q1 2027. Decisions: adopt a 2-week rotating ops bench, standardize incident runbooks, and run a January DR (disaster recovery) dress rehearsal. Owners assigned for runbooks and DR plan.
next_steps: Marco to circulate ops bench sizing spreadsheet and cost model (by 2027-01-05)
Jenna to publish runbook template and run a runbook workshop (by 2027-01-12)
Lena to schedule DR dress rehearsal for January week 3 and invite stakeholders (by 2026-12-27)
Priya to lead on-call rotation pilot for two weeks starting 2027-01-09
action_items: Owen: budget impact summary for ops bench (due 2026-12-30)
questions: How will the ops bench affect committed vs burst capacity billing?
Do we need an emergency recruiting plan if bench headcount gets pulled into incidents?
What metrics will trigger enlarging or shrinking the bench?
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: good morning everyone, thanks for joining the year end -- uh -- maintain and mobilize session. we wanted this to be short and tactical, 45-ish minutes plus q&a. Marco, quick status on the ops bench idea?
[00:22] Marco Ruiz: yeah thanks lena. so the ops bench is basically warm standby capacity — not full reserved clusters but pre-warmed nodes that can be sized quickly. we've run a few microbenchmarks, latency delta is about 8-12% when warming cold vs bench, average spin-up time 90 seconds. caveat: metrics depend on model length and kv cache priming.
[01:05] Kai Nguyen: wait 90 seconds seems long for customer-facing timeouts, are we expecting fallback routes during that spin?
[01:12] Marco Ruiz: good call, kai. the plan is layered: route to lower-cost variant (quantized) if spin > 30s, fallback to secondary region if still constrained. that routing policy will be in the runbook.
[01:35] Priya Sharma: also we need to be explicit about who pagers when bench scales — last time there was confusion and two teams assumed others were on it.
[01:45] Lena Ortiz: agreed. proposing a 2-week rotating bench lead — that person owns the waveform for that block and will be the escalation contact.
[01:55] Owen Brooks: budget question — ops bench = new line item, how do we classify it? is it committed or op-ex?
[02:04] Jenna Li: finance thinks we book it as an on-demand reserve with a monthly baseline cost plus burst buffer. owen, can you prototype a bucketed cost view tied to usage?
[02:14] Owen Brooks: yeah i'll sketch something and share.
[02:20] Lena Ortiz: on incident runbooks, jenna has a template. jenna walk us through the major sections.
[02:28] Jenna Li: sure. top of runbook: detection signals, run-state checklist, stakeholders & rotations, mitigation steps, communication templates, rollback decision triggers, and postmortem timeline. we want a 30-minute detection-to-action loop for p0s.
[02:48] Sara Gomez: will this be mandatory for new hires on the ops bench? training implications?
[02:54] Lena Ortiz: yes; new SREs will get a bench onboarding module during week one. also we'll align career ladder expectations.
[03:05] Marco Ruiz: technical deep-dive: for private deployments and Dedicated customers, the bench concept maps to pre-provisioned pools in customer VPCs. we need a standardized gating checklist for security and KMS access. open question: do we allow auto-scale in VPC without manual approval?
[03:30] Priya Sharma: for regulated customers I'd say manual approval but with a fast path.
[03:35] Lena Ortiz: ok flag that as policy decision.
[03:40] Kai Nguyen: on DR dress rehearsal — what scenario are we practicing? multiregion outage or model regression?
[03:46] Marco Ruiz: both. we want a combined scenario: primary region degraded due to network partition and a hot model regression triggered by a bad rollout. test will exercise routing fallbacks, bench spin-up, rollback cadence, and customer communication.
[04:02] Jenna Li: timeline: dress rehearsal week 3 January, runbook dry run week 2.
[04:09] Owen Brooks: make sure product and sales get communication templates; last time customers were surprised.
[04:15] Lena Ortiz: noted. also we'll create a short customer-facing status page template.
[04:21] (short crosstalk)
[04:30] Priya Sharma: hiring ask — bench increases ops load; proposal: two 0.6 FTE SRE contractors to start, then reassess.
[04:40] Owen Brooks: budget might allow one FTE and one contractor; i'll run numbers.
[04:45] Lena Ortiz: quick poll — is the group comfortable with the rotating 2-week bench lead?
[04:50] Sara Gomez: yes from people ops perspective.
[04:53] Kai Nguyen: yes from eng.
[04:55] Marco Ruiz: yes.
[04:58] Lena Ortiz: good. ok go-to actions recap: marco ops bench sizing, jenna runbook template, priya lead DR playbook, owen budget summary, lena schedule DR. you'll get calendar invites and a link to the ops bench spreadsheet in the notes.
[05:15] Jenna Li: one more note — we'll publish a short FAQ for customers on how fallback routing impacts SLAs.
[05:22] Lena Ortiz: thanks. any final q's?
[05:26] (silence)
[05:30] Lena Ortiz: alright we'll close. thanks team, enjoy the break, and let's be ready for a busy January.
[05:38] (meeting ended)

Notes: referenced artifacts: ops-bench-sizing.xlsx (internal link: drive.redwood/ops/bench/2026-sizing), runbook-template.md (link: drive.redwood/ops/runbooks/template-v2), Q1-ops-priorities deck (link: drive.redwood/decks/q1-ops-2027).
